19 A rubber cord hangs from a rigid support. A weight attached to its lower end is gradually
increased from zero, and then gradually reduced to zero.

The force–extension curve for contraction is below the force–extension curve for stretching.
What does the shaded area between the curves represent?
A
the elastic potential energy stored in the rubber cord
B
the thermal energy dissipated in the rubber cord
C
the work done on the rubber cord during stretching
D
the work done by the rubber cord during contraction
© UCLES 2019
9702/12/O/N/19

hints: Notice the upper stretching arrow and the lower contraction arrow form a closed hysteresis loop with shaded area between them.
Recall that area under a force-extension graph equals work done, so compare the larger area under stretching with the smaller area under contraction.
Think about what happens to the missing energy that is put in on loading but not returned on unloading in rubber.
walkthrough: Identify the two areas to the extension axis: area under the stretching curve is $W_{in} = \int F dx$ for loading, and area under the contraction curve is $W_{out} = \int F dx$ for unloading.
Because the contraction curve lies below the stretching curve, $W_{out}$ is smaller than $W_{in}$ for the same change in extension.
Subtract the two areas: $W_{in} - W_{out}$ leaves exactly the shaded area enclosed between the curves.
Energy is conserved, so the work not recovered as useful mechanical work is dissipated inside the rubber as thermal energy warming the cord.
That net lost energy is represented by the hysteresis loop area. This is option B

A.explanation: Elastic potential energy stored would be related to work recovered on contraction, not the difference between the two curves.

B.explanation: The loop area is work put in minus work got back, so it is energy lost from the cord as thermal energy due to hysteresis.

C.explanation: Work done on the cord during stretching is the total area under the upper stretching curve to the extension axis, not just the shaded strip.

D.explanation: Work done by the cord during contraction is the total area under the lower contraction curve to the extension axis, not just the shaded strip.
